content:
Most asteroids can be easily predicted in their movement. They generally move at a certain speed and direction based on external influences, such as gravity or solar radiation pressure.

However, the asteroid named '1998 KY26' (1998 KY26) is not like that.

This asteroid is unexpectedly accelerating at a high speed like a rebellious character. Its behavior is very different from the natural movement a normal asteroid should exhibit.

One hypothesis about this strange space activity was that this object is only on the surface of an asteroid. In reality, a 'dark comet' might be hidden inside, from which invisible gas is pushing it in a different direction. But now, that hypothesis has been questioned.

According to Corbin Hansen and Masatoshi Hirabayashi, aerospace engineers at 'Georgia Institute of Technology', this 11-meter (36-foot) long space rock is extremely hot. Therefore, it is unlikely that the ice necessary for acceleration can be preserved in it.

The main characteristic of a comet is the ice it contains. Scientists adopted a simple method to check its true identity – measuring its temperature.

In their research paper published in the journal 'Icarus', they wrote, 'The results of our temperature model show a very high rate of water evaporation in 1998 KY26. This means that the ice trapped inside cannot last long. This discovery has further clarified our understanding of the internal structure of asteroids.'

These objects orbiting the solar system mainly fall into two categories – asteroids and comets. Asteroids are mostly large pieces of rock. Comets, on the other hand, contain ice, which turns into vapor and spreads into space as they orbit the sun. The gas escaping in this way provides an additional push beyond gravity, increasing the comet's speed.

When we think of comets, we imagine an object with a bright tail. But not all comets are like that. The activities of objects that scientists call 'dark comets' are not visible from the outside.

Like normal comets, gas is released from them, but a bright tail does not form. Therefore, although they appear like normal asteroids, their speed is somewhat higher.

It was suspected that KY26 might be one such object. This small asteroid rotates on its axis once every 5.35 minutes, and its speed appears to be increasing unusually perpendicular to its orbital plane. For this reason, scientists considered it in the category of dark comets.

The main characteristic of a comet is the ice it contains. Scientists adopted a simple method to check its true identity – measuring its temperature.

Hansen and Hirabayashi did exactly that. They studied the size, orbit, light-reflecting ability, and potential physical structure of KY26 to create a model of its surface and internal temperature.

This research has been published in the science journal 'Icarus'.

To preserve subsurface ice for a long time, the temperature must be below approximately 145 Kelvin (minus 128 degrees Celsius). However, researchers have found that even the coldest part of KY26 reaches an average temperature of at least 212 Kelvin (minus 61 degrees Celsius) during its orbit around the sun. While this is extremely cold for human life, it is very hot for ice to remain.

At such high temperatures, if even 1% of KY26's total mass were ice, it would have completely sublimated within 2,000 years. If that ice were the cause of its unusual speed, it would have been depleted in just 62 years.

KY26 could be billions of years old. However, it is not yet clear when this object arrived in its current orbit. Therefore, it cannot be said that it cannot contain ice, but this latest result and previous studies indicating its origin from the main asteroid belt make that possibility very weak.

So, what is pushing KY26 off its regular path?

The main reason could be solar radiation pressure. The subtle but powerful force generated by sunlight may be forcing this asteroid to change its path and increase its speed.

It is likely that the real truth of this mystery will be revealed soon. Japan's space agency's 'Hayabusa-2' spacecraft is heading towards KY26, which will reach near this object in July 2031. After that, it will not be able to hide its mystery for long.

This research has been published in the science journal 'Icarus'.
